topics: Benchmark summary: Redwood vs baseline provider
Latency tail behavior and p95/p99 differences
Throughput scaling and sustained run results
Tuning knobs: batching, KV cache, quantization
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run about 45 minutes. quick agenda - Milo will walk through this week's benchmark runs versus your baseline, then Q&A, then next steps.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Sounds good, thanks. we've got Maya and Oliver on from infra. Sofia might drop questions on procurement.
[00:20] Milo Chen: Cool, hi all. quick note first, transcription may misstate some names or product terms, so apologies. okay slide-free: summary of runs - we ran three profiles this week: "small chat" (short tokens), "search-ish" (longer context, embeddings+rank), and "sustained throughput". baseline provider is what you shared - their vm pool with 8xA100-ish equiv.
[00:45] Maya Singh: yes that's the one, run id baseline-2026-06-03. their reported p50/p95 were in the sheet.
[00:52] Milo Chen: right. For Redwood on the small-chat profile, p50 about 55ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms; baseline provider p50 ~70ms, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~450ms. so we saw better tail with our runtime, likely due to continuous batching + KV prefix cache.
[01:20] Raj Patel: those look good on p95. how many concurrent RPS were you running?
[01:25] Milo Chen: small-chat was 80 RPS sustained across 10 clients. throughput mode we pushed to 350 RPS to see saturation. baseline saturated at ~290 RPS in your config, Redwood plateaued around 420 before autoscale kicked a different behavior - but note those numbers are with our default quantization profile q4f16 for that model.
[01:48] Oliver Grant: when you say quantization, is that affecting quality? we ran a few eval prompts and saw slight token differences.
[01:55] Milo Chen: good call, yes q4f16 has negligible quality delta for most prompts, but we keep a tuned eval set. we can run q8 and fp16 permutations; the tradeoff is latency/throughput vs tiny accuracy deltas. we ran a quick rouge-like check and saw <0.6% delta on your evals.
[02:18] Maya Singh: can you clarify KV cache behavior - baseline provider said they don't do prefix caching at request-level, it's per-session.
[02:25] Milo Chen: exactly, our runtime does automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts and shared contexts - that cuts tokens per request and reduces compute. for those runs we enabled it where applicable which explains part of the tail improvement. note: we can disable caching to give apples-to-apples but it will increase tokens/latency.
[02:45] Raj Patel: okay, can you share both runs with and without KV-cache?
[02:49] Milo Chen: yes, we'll add those, and include the raw logs.
[02:54] Lena Ortiz: quick procurement note - Sofia, we can follow up with a pricing snapshot for Dedicated vs hosted for your projected 1M monthly tokens.
[03:03] Sofia Ramos: yes please, want to see committed monthly pricing and SLA differences. also curious about data residency for EU and audit logs.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: we'll send the security pack link and SOC2/ISO certs.
[03:14] Milo Chen: back to benchmarks - sustained throughput test: we saw more stable scaling on Redwood because of smarter batching kernels and kernel selection per sequence length. baseline had higher jitter especially under bursty requests which pushes p99 out.
[03:31] Maya Singh: do you have charts for jitter/p95 over time? we look for performance stability not just averages.
[03:37] Milo Chen: yep, attached chart in the sheet - you can see p95 over a 30-minute window; Redwood curve is flatter in regions 10-25m. I'll point you to timestamps in the CSV.
[03:48] Raj Patel: why the difference? is it hardware scheduling or software batching?
[03:52] Milo Chen: both. our runtime pipeline does continuous batching with shaped kernels that keep the GPU saturated without large queue spikes. plus we tune kernel selection, e.g., fused attention kernels for medium sequences. baseline seemed to fall back to a generic kernel under load.
[04:07] Oliver Grant: what about memory - any OOMs during the runs?
[04:10] Milo Chen: none on Redwood. we saw one transient OOM on baseline during the 350 RPS push which triggered retries and increased p99.
[04:18] Maya Singh: can you also run tests with our heavy-context scenario - 2k tokens? last time both systems degraded but we need exact numbers.
[04:25] Milo Chen: yes, we'll add a long-context run. that'll show memory and kernel selection differences.
[04:30] Raj Patel: cost side - your per-token cost in the sheet looks lower but it's not entirely apples-to-apples because baseline included preemptible pricing and different instance mixes.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: correct, so Milo will produce a normalized cost calc - same model, same effective GPU-hour cost, we show per-100k token unit economics and include quantization impact.
[04:50] Milo Chen: also worth noting that for Dedicated pools we can price-optimise by committing capacity - that'll change the cost delta substantially if you commit.
[04:58] Sofia Ramos: we'll want that in the deck. Procurement likes committed/discount comparisons.
[05:02] Raj Patel: network latency matters for us because our app has a microservice call prior to the model call. Were your tests run in us-east region?
[05:10] Milo Chen: tests were run in us-east1. we can re-run in eu-west1 to match your staging. but note network-induced p50 differences will be apparent; we typically recommend colocating inference or using Private/VPC for production to reduce those hops.
[05:25] Maya Singh: about private deployment - we asked about on-prem and our compliance team asked how much performance loss we'd expect versus hosted.
[05:33] Milo Chen: good Q. worst-case, on-prem with identical GPUs should have comparable performance; differences come from networking, autoscaling behavior, and whether you use our managed private control plane. we can set up a benchmark on a small private node to show parity - probably within 5-10% if kernel/driver stack is tuned.
[05:51] Raj Patel: that's promising. any gotchas for our infra team?
[05:53] Milo Chen: driver versions, CUDA, and NCCL tuning matter; we'll share a checklist. also KMS integrations for keys and audit log forwarding are typical items.
[06:04] Oliver Grant: can we get the checklist and the exact docker images?
[06:07] Milo Chen: yes, we'll share container image tags and the infra checklist in the follow-up.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: back to the data - Milo, could you summarize the key numbers we want Raj to look at?
[06:16] Milo Chen: sure: small-chat profile: Redwood p50 55ms vs baseline 70ms; p95 180ms vs 260ms. sustained throughput: Redwood handled 420 RPS vs baseline 290 RPS before qdrops; cost per 100k tokens normalized: Redwood $X (we'll compute exact) vs baseline $Y in your sheet, preliminary looks like 12-18% cost savings depending on quantization choices. long-context (2k tokens) - pending run, expect p50 ~450ms p95 ~1.1s but we'll have exact soon.
[06:47] Maya Singh: when you say qdrops what happened?
[06:49] Milo Chen: baseline had a degradation mode where latency increased sharply when their batch queue hit certain thresholds; we saw retries and backoffs which cost retries and pushed p99.
[06:58] Raj Patel: okay makes sense. can you provide the raw CSVs and the JMeter-like config?
[07:02] Milo Chen: yes, we'll put everything in the shared folder and annotate the CSV with run IDs and timestamps.
[07:08] Sofia Ramos: procurement question, if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum term? 6 months or annual?
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: usually we do annual for biggest discounts, but 6-month trial reserved pools are possible. I'll include the options in the pricing email.
[07:19] Raj Patel: any regulatory concerns if we push to EU?
[07:21] Lena Ortiz: we have SOC2 and ISO certs; for data residency we can deploy control plane in EU and enforce data-at-rest KMS keys you control. we'll send the architecture doc.
[07:31] Milo Chen: last technical note - we recommend enabling intelligent batching + a moderate KV cache TTL for your workload. for chat-like traffic it reduces tokens and latency. For search-like workloads we recommend a slightly larger batch size and the fused-kernel profile. We'll include recommended config snippets.
[07:50] Maya Singh: OK, please include the exact CLI flags or config map we can drop into our test harness.
[07:55] Milo Chen: will do.
[07:57] Lena Ortiz: looks like we're near time. quick recap: Milo will run the 30m sustained test and long-context run, provide CSVs and charts; Maya to share baseline raw logs and workload script; Lena to send pricing + security docs; we'll schedule a deep dive on private deployment next week.
[08:15] Raj Patel: thanks, that works.
[08:18] Sofia Ramos: thanks all.
[08:20] Milo Chen: thanks everyone, I'll follow up with annotated runs.
[08:24] [call ends]
